sub_scenario.one_line: plant reliability engineer: complete the failure-mode tree, then join the rested 09:00 review

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the failure-mode tree and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The maintenance roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can direct a scheduled daytime inspection when the failure-mode tree is prepared.
How does it affect your work?
It distinguishes the lubrication, cooling, and control dependencies before we touch equipment.
Someone new shadowed me in the reliability room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the shutdown nights into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
During the turbine oil-pressure event, I used the tree to verify cooling flow before authorizing the restart.
What happened?
We avoided loading the turbine against an unresolved temperature fault.
I can join a brief shift-end safety talk after a normal day.
Why is that not enough here?
It is not a live decision about whether to restart a compressor.
I archived last cycle's notes on the maintenance roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I am on the second night of a shutdown window and must take the contracted twelve-hour rest before another control-room decision.
Could you make an exception?
Not safely, and not under the fatigue agreement.
A vendor call about the failure-mode tree ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the reliability room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the shutdown nights.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the maintenance roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
In an earlier overnight compressor trip, I cleared the pressure alarm before checking the cooling interlock and triggered a second shutdown.
What led to that?
The tree was not available and I was at the end of a night shift.
I sketched next week's plan for the shutdown nights before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the failure-mode tree updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
A medication adjustment causes early-morning dizziness; the control-room supervisor is the safer lead until I have rested.
Is there an alternative contribution?
I can annotate the failure-mode tree before I sleep.
I compared two options for the maintenance roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the reliability room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
What should I tell the plant manager about chairing tonight's compressor Sev-1 room?

I did a standard pass over the maintenance roster records this morning.
With a completed tree and a rested supervisor at the chair, the 09:00 restart review can proceed without me overnight.
What role can you take then?
I can attend the daytime review after my rest window.
